name: Thursday
label: Victory
lede: A New Brunswick basement band made one of the records that defined emo on a $1.2 million argument with Victory Records, broke up, nearly lost its singer to heroin, and came back anyway.

eras.title: New Year's Eve in Geoff's basement
eras.text: Thursday came out of the New Brunswick, New Jersey basement circuit, where hardcore kids and Smiths fans were the same people. A Rutgers student with a saxophone background met a guitarist at an Ink & Dagger show and ended up the singer.

years.h: Tom Keeley and Tucker Rule start Thursday; Geoff Rickly joins
years.p: Geoff Rickly met Tom Keeley at an [[Ink & Dagger|5f71179f-99af-4f7c-9918-cfb8ad0e39d7]] show and joined months after Keeley and drummer Tucker Rule began. Tim Payne (bass) and Bill Henderson (guitar) complete the band.

years.h: Thursday's first show: Rickly's basement, New Year's Eve
years.p: The bill in Geoff Rickly's New Brunswick basement: Thursday, [[Midtown|1165d619-d5d5-497e-b1b7-261d1e355d96]], [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]] and [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]].

years.h: Waiting on Eyeball Records
years.p: Thursday's debut, with original guitarist Bill Henderson, comes out on the small New Jersey label Eyeball with no singles, radio or video behind it.

years.h: Steve Pedulla replaces Bill Henderson; Thursday signs to Victory
years.p: With Steve Pedulla on guitar, Thursday leaves Eyeball for Chicago's Victory Records and heads into Big Blue Meenie in Jersey City in November.

eras.title: Full Collapse, and whoopee cushions
eras.text: Full Collapse sold 800 copies its first week and then just kept selling. Thursday grew up fast on Victory, and so did the band's list of grievances with founder Tony Brummel.

q: Full Collapse was a record that changed the course and shape of my life.
years.h: Full Collapse: 800 copies in week one, 380,000 by 2008
years.p: Recorded in 20 days with producer Sal Villanueva. Victory shipped 3,400; by October 2008 it had sold 380,000.
years.xp:
Understanding in a Car Crash went to college radio in April, and its video sat in MTV2 rotation for eight weeks. Geoff Rickly has said it's about a car accident involving his girlfriend and his best friend, with a nod to Joy Division.

Critics split: AbsolutePunk gave it 95%, Pitchfork 5.6. Kerrang!, NME and Rolling Stone later put it among the greatest emo albums ever made.

years.h: Thursday plays the 2001 Warped Tour
years.p: The first Warped summer for Thursday, the year Full Collapse came out.

years.h: Victory makes Thursday whoopee cushions for Warped Tour
years.p: Victory's marketing staff produced Thursday-branded whoopee cushions to promote Full Collapse, without the band's consent. They were pulled after Thursday objected.

years.h: Thursday tells fans not to buy Five Stories Falling
years.p: At shows, Thursday urged fans to skip the Victory EP Five Stories Falling. Tony Brummel had also pushed back on the cost of elaborate artwork for Full Collapse.

q: When we parted ways with Victory, we got our asses kicked.
years.src: Wikipedia: Thursday (band) · Wikipedia: Full Collapse · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Thursday goes public with its Victory grievances, and signs to Island
years.p: In a May 2002 statement, Thursday said Tony Brummel's interest was all sales, no art. Island Def Jam signed the band after a bidding war, paying Victory $1.2 million per Geoff Rickly.
years.xp:
The deal was announced in late May 2002 and made official on September 9, 2002, once the exit terms were settled. Island bought out Victory's claim on two more albums, and the Victory logo had to appear on Thursday's next two records.

Relations later thawed: Wikipedia notes Brummel and Victory eventually welcomed Thursday "back with open arms." By then Full Collapse had sold 111,000 copies.

years.h: Thursday headlines the Plea for Peace Tour
years.p: The fall 2002 run comes weeks after the Island deal is finalized.

years.h: Geoff Rickly produces [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]]'s debut
years.p: Rickly produced I Brought You My Bullets, You Brought Me Your Love for the New Jersey band, which later named Thursday as an influence.

eras.title: Top 10 on a major, and burnout
eras.text: Thursday's first Island record debuted in the Top 10 and sent them on tour with AFI, Deftones and Thrice. By 2004 label pressure, touring and health problems had them stepping off.

years.h: War All the Time debuts at No. 7
years.p: Thursday's Island debut sold 74,000 copies in its first week. Andrew Everding's keyboards are on it; he's made an official member in December 2004.

years.h: Thursday takes a break
years.p: The band cited label pressure, relentless touring and health problems. Geoff Rickly has epilepsy, which has affected Thursday's touring.

years.h: Thursday returns for the CBGB benefit, streamed live
years.p: Thursday's comeback show is a benefit for the Bowery club CBGB, then fighting to keep its lease.

years.h: A City by the Light Divided with Dave Fridmann
years.p: The first Thursday album not produced by Sal Villanueva. It's also their last for Island, which the band left early in 2007.
play: A City by the Light Divided

eras.title: Epitaph, then the end
eras.text: Thursday moved to Epitaph, headlined Taste of Chaos and made its most abrasive records. In November 2011 it called time, and Geoff Rickly later said hiatus was the wrong word.

years.h: Common Existence on Epitaph
years.p: Thursday signed to Epitaph Records on September 30, 2008, and headlined the 2009 Taste of Chaos tour behind this album.

years.h: No Devolución, the last album before the breakup
years.p: Thursday's sixth studio album, and the last before the band ended in November 2011.

years.h: Thursday announces it can't continue
years.p: The band said personal circumstances made it impossible to go on in the spirit that made Thursday special. In January 2013 Geoff Rickly said they had in fact disbanded.

years.h: Thursday's last show: Soundwave Festival, Perth, Australia
years.p: The final show of the original run happens on the far side of the world from New Brunswick.

eras.title: Heroin, Shkreli, and a way back
eras.text: Apart, Thursday's members scattered into other bands. Geoff Rickly fell into heroin addiction, got mugged and poisoned on the road, and lost his label to a scandal. The reunion is what he credits with pulling him out.

years.h: Geoff Rickly is mugged in New York
years.p: Two years later he's poisoned and robbed in Hamburg, Germany. Rickly was addicted to heroin through the years Thursday was apart.

years.h: Geoff Rickly forms No Devotion with ex-Lostprophets members
years.p: Rickly also keeps his powerviolence project United Nations going. In the same years, Tucker Rule tours as a drummer with The Wanted and [[Yellowcard|3630fff3-52fc-4e97-ab01-d68fd88e4135]].

years.h: Martin Shkreli is revealed as Collect Records' backer
years.p: Geoff Rickly's label, founded in 2009, had pharma executive Martin Shkreli as a silent investor. Rickly cut ties within days, and the label lost its funding.

years.h: Thursday reunites for Atlanta's Wrecking Ball Festival
years.p: Announced in March for August. Geoff Rickly said the band had reconciled its differences after five years of barely speaking. The reunion helped him get clean.

years.h: Thursday's homecoming at Starland Ballroom
years.p: The New Jersey homecoming show at Sayreville's Starland Ballroom, announced in June.

eras.title: Signals over the air, again
eras.text: The reunion was meant to end in 2019 and didn't. Thursday opened for My Chemical Romance, played its records front to back, replaced two founders on the road and, thirteen years on, released new songs.

years.h: Thursday headlines Brooklyn's Northside Festival
years.p: Part of a 24-date 2017 tour announced in January.

years.h: The planned farewell at Saint Vitus, Brooklyn
years.p: Thursday said in October 2018 the reunion would end in 2019. Instead the band added European dates and played Full Collapse and War All the Time in full at London's Electric Ballroom in December.

years.cap: Opening for My Chemical Romance, Los Angeles, 2019
years.h: Thursday opens [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]]'s reunion show in LA
years.p: The band Geoff Rickly produced back in 2002 invites Thursday to open its first show back.

years.h: Thursday's virtual Signals shows
years.p: Through April 2021 Thursday streams three Signals shows, with guests including [[Frank Iero|358db9a2-3c78-4afb-93b5-d18b34b86eab]], [[Jim Ward|da9ed660-3aef-4c2d-bcc0-89e512696baf]], [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] and Bartees Strange.

years.h: Norman Brannon and Stu Richardson replace Keeley and Payne
years.p: Thursday is now Geoff Rickly, Steve Pedulla and Tucker Rule, with [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]]'s Norman Brannon and No Devotion's Stu Richardson touring. They headline Philadelphia's This Is Hardcore playing Full Collapse.

years.h: Geoff Rickly's novel Someone Who Isn't Me
years.p: An autofictional account of his heroin addiction and experimental treatment with ibogaine.

years.h: Application for Release From the Dream: new Thursday
years.p: Thursday's first new song in 13 years. White Bikes, recorded at Hansa Studio in Berlin and about the death of a friend of Rickly's, follows December 6.

years.h: The Full City Devolución tour, with Chris Conley
years.p: Marking Full Collapse at 25, A City by the Light Divided at 20 and No Devolución at 15, with [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]]'s Chris Conley. It wrapped April 30 in Boston.
